cards.explanation: The answer is the LORD. The burden says “…the eyes of men and of all the tribes of Israel are upon the LORD…” (Zechariah 9:1). Hadrach and Damascus are the first names on the list, and right away the message says where everybody is looking.

The answer is that He will make her poor. The text says, “Behold, the Lord will impoverish her…” (Zechariah 9:4). Tyre had silver like dust and gold like the dirt of the streets. Then the Lord says He'll cast her wealth into the sea.

The answer is False, friends. Tyre built a fortress and heaped up silver and gold (Zechariah 9:3), but the verse says she will be consumed by fire (Zechariah 9:4). The text doesn't say the fortress keeps her safe. Fire is what's coming.

The answer is False. When Ashkelon sees what happens to Tyre, the text says, “Ashkelon will see and fear…” (Zechariah 9:5). Fear is the word for Ashkelon, not celebration. Gaza will writhe in agony, as will Ekron, in the same verse.
The answer is True, friends. The verse says, “There will cease to be a king in Gaza…” (Zechariah 9:5). Gaza is named right alongside Ashkelon and Ekron in that verse. Its king is part of what goes.

The answer is their pride, bakers. The LORD says, “…I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.” (Zechariah 9:6). A mixed race will occupy Ashdod. Then the verse names pride as the thing being cut off.

The answer is a remnant for God, friends. After the blood and the abominations are removed from their mouths, the text says, “Then they too will become a remnant for our God…” (Zechariah 9:7). The Philistines are described as God's remnant. That's quite a turn.
The answer is Judah! The text says the Philistines “…will become like a clan in Judah…” (Zechariah 9:7). They go from the burden list to being likened to a clan. And that clan is in Judah.

The answer is that He keeps watch with His own eyes, bakers. The LORD says, “…never again will an oppressor overrun My people, for now I keep watch with My own eyes.” (Zechariah 9:8). The promise rests on the LORD watching with His own eyes. The verse gives no other reason.

The answer is True. The text says, “Rejoice greatly, O Daughter of Zion! Shout in triumph, O Daughter of Jerusalem!” (Zechariah 9:9). The reason comes in the next line: “See, your King comes to you…” After all the burden talk, this is a big change of mood.
The answer is a donkey, friends. The King is “…humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.” (Zechariah 9:9). A righteous and victorious King, and the verse puts Him on a donkey.

The answer is that it will be broken, bakers. The text says, “…the bow of war will be broken.” (Zechariah 9:10). The chariot is cut off from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem. The bow goes with them.
The answer is peace! The text says, “Then He will proclaim peace to the nations.” (Zechariah 9:10). The chariot is cut off and the bow of war is broken. Then the King's message is peace.

The answer is False. The text says, “His dominion will extend from sea to sea, and from the Euphrates to the ends of the earth.” (Zechariah 9:10). It doesn't stop at Jerusalem. It reaches to the ends of the earth.

The answer is that He will release them, friends. The LORD speaks: “As for you, because of the blood of My covenant, I will release your prisoners from the waterless pit.” (Zechariah 9:11). The prisoners are in a waterless pit. Because of the blood of His covenant, they are released.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “Return to your stronghold, O prisoners of hope…” (Zechariah 9:12). The prisoners are released in verse 11, and the next verse gives them a direction. They aren't just released, they're told where to go.

The answer is Zion, bakers. The LORD is speaking, and He says, “I will rouse your sons, O Zion, against the sons of Greece.” (Zechariah 9:13). Just before that, He says He will bend Judah as His bow and fit it with Ephraim. So the sons here are Zion's sons.

The answer is the sword of a mighty man, friends. The LORD says, “I will make you like the sword of a mighty man.” (Zechariah 9:13). Earlier in the verse He says He will bend Judah as His bow. So Judah is as a bow, and Zion will be like a sword.

The answer is lightning! The text says, “Then the LORD will appear over them, and His arrow will go forth like lightning.” (Zechariah 9:14). The LORD appears over them. His arrow is likened to lightning.

The answer is that He will shield them, bakers. The text says, “The LORD of Hosts will shield them.” (Zechariah 9:15). The ram's horn is in the verse right before it (Zechariah 9:14). In verse 15, the LORD of Hosts is the one who shields.

The answer is True. The text says, “…they will be filled like sprinkling bowls, drenched like the corners of the altar.” (Zechariah 9:15). The people are likened to bowls that are full. And they're drenched like the corners of the altar.

The answer is jewels, friends! The text says, “…like jewels in a crown they will sparkle over His land.” (Zechariah 9:16). Jewels are the picture of how His people will shine. The verse says the LORD their God will save them as the flock of His people.

The answer is False, friends. The last verse says, “How lovely they will be, and how beautiful! Grain will make the young men flourish, and new wine, the young women.” (Zechariah 9:17). They end up lovely and beautiful. The young men and women flourish, and the chapter closes on that.
